reliefVocabulary.primaryReliefTermBasis: The statutory term, and on profile:terminology.allowedStateTerms. profile:terminology.pathwayLabels records 'Order of nondisclosure (Gov't Code Ch. 411) — seals from public, broader reach' as one of the two Texas tools, against 'Expunction (Chapter 55A) — erases the record, non-convictions'.
reliefVocabulary.prohibitedTermsBasis: Nondisclosure seals rather than destroys, and the two remedies have different codes, different venues — the sentencing court rather than the county of arrest — and different effects. profile:terminology.avoidUniversalExpungementLabel is true. Using expunction vocabulary here is the wrong remedy on its face.
prohibitedStatements: That the participant may deny the matter. They may not, in the contexts covered by the Gov't Code 411.0765 agency list.
That the record is destroyed, erased or removed. It is sealed and it remains available to the listed agencies.
That an order covers more than one offence. An order applies to one offence.
That the court will find issuance to be in the best interest of justice. That is the court's finding.
That the state will not request a hearing.

provenance.profileCoverageNote: The compiled TX profile records no pathway, question, ordered decision rule, waiting-period rule, exclusion rule or packetGenerator entry for this section. Its nine pathways are five Chapter 55A expunction routes plus 411.072 automatic nondisclosure, 411.0725 petitioned deferred nondisclosure, 411.0735 conviction nondisclosure and first-offence DWI nondisclosure. Full-value scans return zero hits for '411.0729', 'veterans reemployment' and '42A' subchapter H-1. What the profile supplies, and what is used here, is the expunction-versus-nondisclosure framing, the sealed-not-erased effect, the fact that nondisclosure reaches many situations expunction cannot, and the county-specific-fee statement.
provenance.statePackCoverageNote: The committed Texas state pack carries build metadata and the Nationwide inventory only — three files under 'LegalEase Texas' — and records no track-level filing text, no caption, no vocabulary and no statutory citations. Its officialFormInventory contains neither OCA nondisclosure form.

mechanism: A misdemeanour for which the person was placed on community supervision, including deferred adjudication, who successfully completed all conditions and successfully completed a court-approved veterans reemployment programme under Code of Criminal Procedure Chapter 42A, Subchapter H-1, after committing the offence, and who is a veteran of the United States Armed Forces including reserves, national guard or state guard. Read at source on 2026-08-06: the court shall enter the order after notice to the state and a hearing on whether issuance is in the best interest of justice, and the statute names no filing party — there is no petition requirement in the section. Under 411.0729(b) the section applies regardless of whether the defendant meets the other eligibility criteria in the subchapter, so the Gov't Code 411.074 basic conditions do not gate it. There is no waiting period. OCA nonetheless publishes a model petition and instructions for the section, because in practice courts may require a petition or may not hold the hearing. The section was last amended in 2019 and was not touched in 2025 or 2026.

authoritySpine.description: The section. An order of nondisclosure for a misdemeanour where the person was placed on community supervision, including deferred adjudication, successfully completed all conditions, successfully completed a court-approved veterans reemployment programme under Code of Criminal Procedure Chapter 42A, Subchapter H-1 after committing the offence, and is a veteran of the United States Armed Forces including reserves, national guard or state guard.

Read at source on 2026-08-06: the court SHALL enter the order after notice to the state and a hearing on whether issuance is in the best interest of justice. The statute names no filing party and imposes no petition requirement.

The section applies regardless of whether the defendant meets the other eligibility criteria in the subchapter, so the Gov't Code 411.074 basic conditions do not gate it. A person barred from every other nondisclosure section may still qualify here.

The petition procedure where a petition is used. (b) requires the fee that generally applies to filing a civil case; (c) and (d) direct OCA to prescribe and publish a form for petitions filed electronically or by mail, and require every county and district clerk website to link to it; (e) provides for notice to the state and an opportunity for a hearing, with a hearing required unless the state does not request one before the 45th day after receiving notice and the court finds the person entitled to file and that issuance is in the best interest of justice.

venue.statement: Statewide in scope with court-level filing. The petition is filed with the clerk of the court that sentenced the person or placed the person on community supervision, including deferred adjudication community supervision — not the county of arrest. This is the single biggest venue difference from expunction, and it matters because a person with both an expunction and a nondisclosure may be filing in two different courts.

destination.name: The court that placed the person on community supervision, and its clerk
destination.detail: Statewide mechanism with court-level filing. OCA publishes the model petition, order and instructions statewide; no county form is promoted to statewide status.

waitingPeriods.duration: None. The trigger is successful completion of the programme and of all community-supervision conditions.
The court holds a hearing on whether issuance is in the best interest of justice, and unless it finds issuance is not in the best interest of justice it must enter the order.

units.legalUnit: The order the court owes without any petition. Section 411.0729 names no filing party and imposes no petition requirement: the court holds a hearing and, unless it finds issuance is not in the best interest of justice, enters the order. LegalEase confirms veteran status, successful completion of all community-supervision conditions and of the Subchapter H-1 reemployment programme, and prompts the court to act. Nothing is filed on this route and no filing fee arises. This is the route the registry says to lead with.

omissionProof.statement: units[] enumerates every legal unit that the pinned registry entry and the compiled TX profile record for tx_nd_veterans_reemployment, and adds no unit either source does not record. The registry's own units[] has exactly TWO entries and both are carried, preserving their unitIds and order values: tx-nd0729-no-filing-route (order 1, outputStrategy process_guidance, outputStrategyStatus resolved, packetIdentity unresolved, available true) is unit 1 here, and tx-nd0729-oca-petition (order 2, outputStrategy official_pdf_fill, outputStrategyStatus resolved, packetIdentity identified, available true) is unit 2 here. No third registry unit exists. registry packetSet.components contains exactly FIVE entries and all five are carried, one per unit: components[0] no_filing_route_guidance on unit 1, components[1] petition on unit 2, components[2] proposed_order on unit 3, components[3] fee_waiver_statement on unit 4, components[4] after_order_instructions on unit 5. Units 3, 4 and 5 therefore have componentIds from the registry but no registry units[] parent: unit 3 belongs to the petition alternative and is separated because it is a distinct official form with a distinct URL, acquisition state and manual completion item; unit 4 is conditional inside the petition alternative by its own conditionDescription; unit 5 is marked required with no condition and therefore applies on both alternatives, which is why it cannot be attached to either registry unit. Each carries registryUnitId explicitly, null where none exists, and a registryUnitNote saying so. Nothing in packetSet.participantActionRequired constitutes a separate legal unit: its fifteen entries are three obtain_document and three confirm_answer entries for record gathering, three complete_field manual completion items, one sign, one notarize, one pay_fee, one apply_fee_waiver, one serve_party and one file — and every one is carried inside a unit's participantTreatment, a dependency file, or participant-instructions.md. registry manualCompletionItems has three entries; all three map onto units 2 and 3 rather than describing separate units. registry postGenerationHandoffs is EMPTY, so no unit is drawn from it. No agency_request_letter unit and no cover_sheet unit is created: neither source records a written request document or a cover sheet for this track, and creating either would exceed the source. The compiled profile contributes zero units, because it does not record this section at all.

profilePassageReferenced.passage: Order of nondisclosure (Gov't Code Ch. 411) — seals from public, broader reach. Available for many situations expunction cannot reach, principally completed deferred adjudication and some convictions. Main subtypes: 411.072 — automatic nondisclosure ...; 411.0725 — deferred adjudication (petition) ...; 411.0735 — certain convictions ...; 411.0731 / DWI: first-offense DWI nondisclosure.
profilePassageReferenced.interpretation: This is the profile's complete enumeration of the Gov't Code ch. 411 subtypes and it names FOUR. Section 411.0729 is not among them, and neither 'veterans reemployment' nor 'Subchapter H-1' appears anywhere in the profile. The profile therefore records ZERO legal units for this track, and units[] above cannot be a subset of it — it is a complete image of the registry's own units[] plus its packetSet.components. What the profile does supply, and what is used, is: the two-tool framing and the sealed-versus-erased distinction (sourceSections[1] and [4]); the statement that a nondisclosure order leaves the record visible to a statutory agency list and that the person may not deny it in those contexts (sourceSections[4]); the sample nondisclosure prayer's structure (sourceSections[11]); and the county-specific nondisclosure filing fee (sourceSections[8]).

counselFlags.statement: No petition is required by Gov't Code 411.0729. The court must hold a hearing and, unless it finds issuance is not in the best interest of justice, must enter the order. The registry's controlling instruction is to LEAD WITH THE NO-FILING ROUTE. A packet that opens with the OCA petition would sell a participant a filing and a fee the statute does not require.
counselFlags.mustConfirm: That the participant-facing flow presents the no-filing route first in every case and reaches the petition only on courtRequiresPetition = yes or a hearing that did not happen.

counselFlags.statement: The Gov't Code 411.074 basic conditions DO NOT apply to this section. Under 411.0729(b) the section applies regardless of whether the defendant meets the other eligibility criteria in the subchapter. A person barred from every other nondisclosure section may still qualify here, and screening must not import the 411.074 bars. This is the single most consequential screening instruction on the track and it points the opposite way from every sibling nondisclosure track.
counselFlags.mustConfirm: That the shared nondisclosure screening does not apply 411.074 bars to this section.

counselFlags.statement: Nondisclosure venue is the SENTENCING COURT, not the county of arrest. The petition is filed with the clerk of the court that sentenced the person or placed them on community supervision, including deferred adjudication. The registry calls this the single biggest venue difference from expunction and notes that a person with both an expunction and a nondisclosure may be filing in two different courts.
counselFlags.mustConfirm: That sentencingCourt, not arrestCounty, drives venue on every nondisclosure track.

counselFlags.statement: The OCA nondisclosure documents are statewide MODEL forms — not mandatory, not promulgated. Confirmed 2026-08-06 from the Texas Judicial Branch nondisclosure forms page and from the document footers themselves, which read OCA MODEL PETITION and are dated February 2022, with the Overview dated February 2024. Gov't Code 411.0745(c) and (d) do direct OCA to prescribe and publish a form for petitions filed electronically or by mail, and require every county and district clerk website to link to it, so they sit closer to a statutorily authorised statewide model than to a sample. Nothing in Subchapter E-1 makes the OCA form mandatory or forbids a differently drafted petition, and this artifact does not assert that it is mandatory. It also does not substitute a drafted petition for it: the registry classifies the unit official_pdf_fill with packetIdentity 'identified', and lane C drafts no official forms.
counselFlags.mustConfirm: That the packet never asserts the OCA form is mandatory, and that the decision to use the OCA form rather than a drafted petition is ratified.

All three of its produced artifacts are official forms and all three are handed off: the OCA Model Petition under Section 411.0729, the OCA Model Order under Section 411.0729, and the Rule 145 Statement of Inability. Every one carries sha256 null. Lane C's entire output on this track is the two participant-instruction documents and the dependency records.
counselFlags.mustConfirm: That all three official forms are acquired at current revision, hashed and field-mapped by the official-PDF overlay lane before any packet is assembled.

counselFlags.statement: An order of nondisclosure applies to ONE offence. Multiple offences require multiple orders, and the registry states this is a cost and packet multiplier the participant must be told about BEFORE PAYING. The after-order instructions carry it.
counselFlags.mustConfirm: That a participant with multiple offences is told the multiplier before any payment is taken.

counselFlags.statement: Nondisclosure seals rather than destroys. The record remains available to the criminal justice and noncriminal justice agencies listed in Gov't Code 411.0765, which include school districts, charter and private schools, education service centres and commercial transportation companies, and the person may NOT deny the matter in those contexts. Expunction vocabulary — expunge, expunction, erase, destroy — is prohibited on this track, and so is any statement that the participant may deny the matter.
counselFlags.mustConfirm: That participant copy never promises erasure or destruction and never tells the participant they may deny the matter.

counselFlags.statement: The registry cites Gov't Code 411.0765 as the list of agencies to which a sealed record remains available. The compiled TX profile cites Gov't Code 411.075(b) for the same proposition, twice, and its sample nondisclosure prayer directs DPS 'to seal the record and notify the agencies listed in 411.075(b)'. No source read reconciles the two citations. Nothing in this artifact reproduces either citation as the operative list in a court document, because no court document is drafted here; the participant copy names the categories of agency rather than the section.
counselFlags.mustConfirm: Which section — 411.0765 or 411.075(b) — carries the agency list, and whether the OCA model order's own recital matches.

counselFlags.statement: Under Gov't Code 411.0745(e) the court provides notice to the state and an opportunity for a hearing on receipt of the petition. A hearing is required unless the state does not request one before the 45th day after receiving notice AND the court finds the person entitled to file and that issuance is in the best interest of justice. The filer should not be charged for that notice. None of that is a participant act, and no packet states that notice was given, that the state did or did not request a hearing, or that any finding was made.
counselFlags.mustConfirm: That no pipeline stage asserts notice, the 45-day lapse, the state's position or a best-interest finding.

counselFlags.statement: The registry records two service facts that do not fully agree. rules.service says the COURT notifies the state and that a copy to the prosecuting attorney is included only 'where local practice requires the filer to deliver' one. rules.notice adds that the OCA instructions 'direct the petitioner to show proof that the district attorney received a copy of the petition'. No source read names a county in which the filer must serve, and the OCA instruction sheet itself is one of the February-2022 documents flagged as stale. No certificate of service or proof-of-receipt document is drafted; the participant is told to ask the clerk.
counselFlags.mustConfirm: Whether the OCA instructions still direct the petitioner to show proof of the district attorney's receipt, and in which counties the filer must deliver a copy.

counselFlags.statement: No fee arises on the no-filing route. On the petition route, Gov't Code 411.0745(b) requires the fee that generally applies to filing a civil case, which is county-specific. No figure is quoted anywhere in this artifact. The compiled profile's 'Nondisclosure petition filing — Filing fee + service; District clerk; varies by county' is consistent and equally unquantified.
counselFlags.mustConfirm: That no fee figure is ever printed for this track, and that the no-fee character of the statutory route is stated plainly.

counselFlags.statement: Recorded self-help stop conditions: any family violence finding or family violence allegation anywhere in the record; any prior conviction or deferred adjudication other than a fine-only traffic offence where the target section carries a first-time-offender condition; the prosecutor opposing the petition or requesting a hearing; any dispute about whether the sentence, fines, costs or restitution were completed; immigration consequences; any question whether the offence was violent or sexual in nature, which is a court determination under Gov't Code 411.0735; the court finding that issuance is not in the best interest of justice; and veteran status or Subchapter H-1 completion that cannot be established. Note the tension: 411.0729(b) disapplies the subchapter's other eligibility criteria, yet the first-time-offender stop condition is recorded on this track. No source read resolves whether that stop is a legal bar here or a prudential one.
counselFlags.mustConfirm: Whether the first-time-offender and family-violence stop conditions are legal bars on a section that expressly disapplies the subchapter's other criteria, or prudential stops.

counselFlags.statement: The compiled TX profile records four nondisclosure subtypes — 411.072 automatic, 411.0725 deferred, 411.0735 conviction and the first-offence DWI provisions — and does not mention 411.0729, veterans reemployment programmes or Code of Criminal Procedure ch. 42A subch. H-1 anywhere. Its nine pathways include no veterans-reemployment route. What the profile does supply, and what is used here, is the expunction-versus-nondisclosure framing, the sealed-not-erased effect, the sentencing-court-versus-arrest-county contrast and the county-specific-fee statement. This track rests on the pinned registry entry.
counselFlags.mustConfirm: Whether the TX profile should be regenerated against a corpus that includes Subchapter E-1 in full, including 411.0729.
